claim: Codec E cuts r6's 12-bit W stream to 11.07 bits/weight on the reference weights. That figure includes per-lane padding, the LUT, the escape lists and the offsets; the code alone is 10.86. On the judge's weights it is a 7.8% byte cut on every m <= 16 shape that gv serves at the HBM stream. The decode is about 196 SASS per warp-chunk, 6.1 per weight, against r6's 49 on the same geometry. It should stay hidden at m <= 8, where r6 uses about 20% of issue and a 512-thread CTA keeps 16 decoding warps per SM, so pooler m=1 should fall by about 1.0-1.1 us of stream minus about 0.2 us for the 512-thread geometry. The format is a pair-Huffman code over the 8-bit exponent: <= 8 bits per A register, decoded with one 256-entry LUT (in smem) per mma A register, a per-lane 64-bit bit buffer, and a per-lane cp.async ring of 4 or 8 16-byte pieces. The sign|mantissa byte plane rides in r6's low-byte plane slots, and an 8-bit-XOR variant of r6's escape walk handles escapes. The A fragments, mma, reduction and epilogue are r6's own.
paths: ge-* = gv FMT 4. qkv on r6's judge-picked geometries: m 1/8 1.8.16 with single LUT, lane-replicated LUT (r), ring depth 8 (d8) and fixed stride (f); m16 1.4.8 S4 with single and r; m32 1.4.16 S2 with single. pooler on r6's 512-thread 2.8.16: m 1/8 with single, r, d8 and f; m16 with single, and r at ST1. pooler m32 1.8.16 XS2 at ST1. unpooler: m 1/8 1.4.16 on rows 0..1023 with single and r; m16 1.4.16 XS2 with single and r; m32 at ST1. That is 29 bake paths and 19 instances, all with 0 spills. o and the router are not served, nor is the 1024-thread pooler geometry, which spills at its 64-register cap. Every r6 path, bake and dispatch is unchanged: r6's 78 gv instances are SASS-identical, and kernel_fn takes an E plan only when it beat r6's pick by 1% in the second bake.
target_shapes: pooler m=1 and m=8: >= 0.8 us under r6 in the bake (r6 judge 13.95)
qkv_gate m=1/8 (r6 9.97, 1.83x CTA imbalance stays), unpooler m=1/8 and the m=16 shapes: 0.3-1.0 us each if the decode stays hidden
kill_if: pooler m=1 E path not ≥ 0.8 µs under r6 in the same bake
local_checks: Full gv block, 98 instances, compiled with nvcc 12.8 sm_90a -O3 in 27 s locally (r6 alone takes 14 s). r6's 78 instances are SASS-identical to r6-c12. The 19 E instances all have 0 spills: 112-128 regs, and 119 for pooler m=1 2.8.16. Pooler m=1 E SASS per warp-chunk: 196 instructions, against r6's 49 on the same geometry. The breakdown is 16 LUT LDS [R+UR], 4 ring LDS, 1 predicated LDGSTS + LDGDEPBAR + DEPBAR.LE SB0,2, 4 HMMA, and no LDL/STL. An instruction-level CPU emulation of the FMT-4 data path is bit-exact on the reference weights on every served geometry and variant. It covers generic PRMT/LOP3, the smem ring with early and late landing, the LUT smem image and the escape walk. It found and fixed the study's ce_sel immLut: 0xe4 must be 0xb8. lint ok; cpu-check --official 9/9; the CPU mock of the bake builds every plan.
risks: Decode latency chain: about 30 clk of LDS per pair, serial per lane. At pooler m=1 there are 16 warps/SM on 2.8.16, and if that is not enough the stream gain is lost. The d8 and r variants are the hedges.
Never executed on a GPU: the cp.async ring hazards and the LUT fill/__syncthreads are checked only by emulation.

Prepare time: pw16 took 133 s for the r6 phase (122 gv instances) and 5 s for its bake. pw17 compiles 98 instances, adding about 13 s locally, and runs 7 packs (< 1 s each on CPU, each proven by unpack_e) and 29 bake paths, 10 of them with m=1 one-hot validation (4096-8192 launches each). Expected total about 160 s against the 240 s budget; the bake skips paths past the budget.
